questions.prompt: How do you invoke an anonymous function `add = fn a, b -> a + b end` in Elixir?

code.source:
add = fn a, b -> a + b end
add.(2, 3)

questions.prompt: What does `&(&1 * 2)` represent in Elixir?

options.text: A capture-syntax shorthand for `fn x -> x * 2 end`

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about anonymous functions and closures in Elixir. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Anonymous functions can have multiple pattern-matching clauses
Anonymous functions are invoked with a dot: `fun.(arg)`
Closures capture the values of outer bindings at definition time (immutable snapshot)
Rebinding an outer variable later mutates the captured value inside an existing closure

questions.prompt: Why is tail-call optimization (TCO) important for recursive functions in Elixir?

options.text: When the recursive call is the very last operation, BEAM reuses the current stack frame so deep recursion runs in O(1) stack space
It automatically parallelizes across CPU cores

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between `Enum` and `Stream` in Elixir?

options.text: `Enum` only works on lists and `Stream` only works on maps
`Enum` is eager (executes each step immediately, building intermediate collections), whereas `Stream` is lazy (composes steps and evaluates on demand)

questions.prompt: What does this pipeline return?
In a `for` comprehension, what does the `:into` option do?

options.text: Collects the comprehension's results into any `Collectable` (such as a map `%{}` or binary `""`) instead of a list

questions.prompt: What does the `:reduce` option in `for` comprehensions enable?

options.text: Accumulating a single value across iterations without building an intermediate list

questions.prompt: Match each polymorphism mechanism in Elixir to its primary use case.

columns.label: Data-driven dispatch based on the type of the first argument (e.g., `Enumerable`, `String.Chars`)
Module-level contract specifying functions an implementing module must define (e.g., `GenServer`, `Plug`)
Compile-time checked map with fixed keys and default values

questions.prompt: What does `@enforce_keys [:email]` do before `defstruct [:email, :name]`?

options.text: Makes `:email` required when constructing `%User{...}`, raising `ArgumentError` at compile time if omitted
Validates email format with a regex
Makes `:email` a primary key in Ecto

questions.prompt: When should you return `{:ok, value} | {:error, reason}` vs calling `raise` in Elixir?

options.text: Always `raise` for every expected validation or I/O failure
Return `{:ok, value}` / `{:error, reason}` for expected, recoverable outcomes, and reserve `raise` for programmer bugs or truly exceptional conditions

questions.prompt: In a `with` expression, what is the purpose of an `else` block?

options.text: It runs only when all `<-` clauses succeed
It pattern-matches on any non-matching `<-` result to normalize errors or handle failures in one place

questions.prompt: Match each `try` block clause in Elixir to what it handles.

columns.label: Cleanup that always runs whether `try` succeeds or fails
Runs only if the `try` body succeeds without raising or throwing

questions.prompt: What does "let it crash" mean in Elixir/OTP?

options.text: Avoid defensive try/catch boilerplate for unexpected states; let a supervised process fail fast and restart cleanly to a known-good state
Ignore all errors and never write tests
Crash the entire OS container on any HTTP 404

questions.prompt: What does `<<a::8, b::16, rest::binary>> = <<1, 0, 2, 3, 4>>` bind `a`, `b`, and `rest` to?
Why is IO data (nested lists of strings/bytes like `["hello", [" ", "world"]]`) preferred over repeated `<>` concatenation when building large outputs?

options.text: IO data avoids copying and reallocating intermediate binaries; BEAM writes nested chunks directly to sockets/files

questions.prompt: Select all statements that are true about Elixir's module directives (`alias`, `import`, `require`, `use`). (Select all that apply.)

options.text: `import Enum, only: [map: 2]` brings functions/macros into scope without the module prefix
`require Logger` is needed before calling macros defined in `Logger`
`use GenServer` invokes `GenServer.__using__/1` macro, which can inject code and attributes
`alias MyApp.Accounts.User` lets you refer to `User` instead of the full module name

questions.prompt: In Elixir metaprogramming, what do `quote` and `unquote` do?

options.text: `quote` escapes SQL strings and `unquote` unescapes them
`quote` turns an Elixir expression into its AST representation (3-tuples), and `unquote` injects evaluated values into a `quote` block

questions.prompt: Why is it best practice to keep Elixir macros small and delegate heavy logic to regular functions?

options.text: Macros expand at compile time and are harder to debug and compose; delegating to functions keeps AST generation minimal
Functions are only evaluated at compile time

questions.prompt: How does `defimpl` handle a protocol when you implement it for `Any`?

options.text: It automatically applies to all types with no opt-in
With `@derive MyProtocol` on structs (or `@fallback_to_any true` on the protocol), types without a specific implementation use `Any`

questions.prompt: What is the role of `config/config.exs` vs `config/runtime.exs` in a Mix project?

options.text: `config.exs` runs at runtime and `runtime.exs` runs at compile time
`config.exs` is evaluated at compile time, whereas `runtime.exs` runs at application boot (including inside releases) to read environment variables

questions.prompt: In `mix.exs`, what does `runtime: false` on a dependency like `{:credo, "~> 1.7", only: [:dev, :test], runtime: false}` mean?

options.text: Credo runs in a separate OS container
Credo is downloaded from GitHub at runtime
Credo is compiled for dev/test tooling but its OTP application is not started at runtime

questions.prompt: What does `use ExUnit.Case, async: true` enable for a test module?

options.text: Allows the test module to run concurrently with other `async: true` test modules in separate processes
Runs each `test` block in a browser

questions.prompt: In ExUnit, how do `doctest MyModule` assertions work?

options.text: ExUnit parses `iex>` prompt/output examples inside `@doc` and `@moduledoc` and executes them as unit tests

questions.prompt: What is the main advantage of `Mox` for mocking in Elixir tests?

options.text: It monkey-patches global module definitions across all processes
It defines mocks against explicit `@behaviour` contracts and scopes expectations per-process, keeping `async: true` tests safe

questions.prompt: Match each static-analysis / quality tool in Elixir to what it checks.

questions.prompt: What does `String.to_integer("42")` vs `Integer.parse("42px")` return?

options.text: `String.to_integer("42")` returns `42` (raising on trailing chars), while `Integer.parse("42px")` returns `{42, "px"}`

questions.prompt: What does `defmacro` receive as its arguments when called?

options.text: The evaluated runtime values of the arguments
The quoted AST expressions of the arguments

questions.prompt: Why does `defstruct` NOT automatically implement the `Access` behaviour?

options.text: Structs have fixed compile-time keys, so `user.field` is preferred over dynamic `user[:field]` lookup unless `Access` is explicitly implemented
Structs are immutable and `Access` is mutable

options.text: Loads the entire file into memory as a single string before counting
Reads and counts lines lazily in chunks with bounded memory usage
